descripcion: At B2 speculation is expressed with the most common modal verbs: might, could, will probably. The full speculation chain with a grounding observation and an acknowledged limit (C1) isn't the focus yet — a clearly graded prediction is enough.

ejemplos.texto: It might rain later, so bring a jacket.
This will probably take longer than expected.
It's bound to change again before the end of the year.

notas: Might and could are close in meaning here and both express a real but uncertain possibility.
Probably goes between the subject and the main verb: it will probably happen, not it probably will happen (though both are heard).
Bound to is a strong prediction, close to certain — use it only when you really mean it.

es.en: Spanish predicts with the future or the future of probability (será que…), which can lead to overusing will and avoiding might or could, losing the lower degree of certainty.
es.es: El español predice con el futuro o el futuro de probabilidad («será que…»), lo que puede llevar a usar demasiado «will» y evitar «might» o «could», perdiendo un grado de certeza más bajo.

de.en: German könnte maps well onto could or might, and wird wohl onto will probably. The scale of certainty therefore transfers directly.
de.de: «Könnte» lässt sich gut mit «could» oder «might» wiedergeben, «wird wohl» mit «will probably». Die Abstufung der Sicherheit lässt sich daher gut übertragen.

it.en: The Italian future of probability (sarà a casa) tends to become he will be at home, which sounds more certain than intended. Potrebbe maps well onto might or could.
it.it: Il futuro di probabilità italiano («sarà a casa») tende a diventare «he will be at home», che suona più certo del previsto. «Potrebbe» corrisponde bene a «might» o «could».

fr.en: Il se peut que corresponds to might and il pourrait to could, so the lower degrees of certainty transfer well. The French future maps onto will for firm predictions.
fr.fr: «Il se peut que» correspond à «might» et «il pourrait» à «could», donc les degrés faibles de certitude se transfèrent bien. Le futur français correspond à «will» pour les prédictions fermes.

pt.en: Pode ser que corresponds to might, and vai + infinitive to going to. The scale of certainty therefore transfers well.
pt.pt: «Pode ser que» corresponde a «might», e «vai» + infinitivo a «going to». A escala de certeza, portanto, se transfere bem.

errores: Using only will for every prediction, regardless of certainty.
Using bound to for something that's actually uncertain.

traducciones.de: Es besteht eine gute Chance, dass…
traducciones.fr: Il y a de fortes chances que…

redemittel.expresion: It probably has to do with…

traducciones.de: Das hat vermutlich damit zu tun, dass…
traducciones.it: Probabilmente ha a che fare con…

traducciones.fr: Cela ne peut pas être exact.

traducciones.it: Non ne ho idea, ma forse…

redemittel.expresion: I don't know that for certain.

traducciones.es: Eso no lo sé con certeza.
traducciones.fr: Je ne le sais pas avec certitude.

autochequeo: Have I used more than one modal verb, not just will every time?
Is probably in the right position in the sentence?
Does the level of certainty match how sure I actually am?
Have I used bound to only when genuinely confident?
Are might and could used interchangeably where appropriate?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the modal verbs used for prediction. Check the position of probably and whether the certainty level fits the context. Do not rewrite the text.

es: «*Seguro que viene*» rendered as *Sure that he comes* instead of *He's bound to come*.
de: *Er kommt bestimmt* rendered as *He comes certainly* instead of *He's bound to come*.
it: «*Di sicuro*» rendered as *Of sure* instead of *Definitely* or *He's bound to*.
fr: *C'est sûr qu'il viendra* rendered as *It's sure that he will come* instead of *He's sure to come*.
pt: *De certeza* rendered as *Of certainty* instead of *Definitely*.
